recognize_zh: 左圖可見一顆循環芽細胞（核大、染色質細緻、胞質少而偏藍）緊鄰一顆有核紅血球；右圖的嗜中性球胞質顆粒很少、細胞核分葉異常呈團塊狀。紅血球大小不一並有淚滴狀與橢圓形，符合伴隨過多芽細胞的MDS。
features: Circulating blast: large cell with high N:C ratio, finely dispersed chromatin and a thin rim of basophilic agranular cytoplasm
Adjacent nucleated red blood cell (orthochromatic normoblast) with a dense round pyknotic nucleus
Dysplastic neutrophil (right panel) with hypogranular pale cytoplasm and abnormally clumped, irregularly separated nuclear lobes
Marked anisopoikilocytosis of red cells with teardrop cells, elliptocytes and occasional fragments
Platelets are sparse in both panels
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear (composite of two fields) shows marked red cell anisopoikilocytosis with teardrop cells, elliptocytes and occasional fragmented forms, and platelets are sparse. A circulating blast with finely dispersed chromatin and scant basophilic agranular cytoplasm is present adjacent to a nucleated red blood cell. A neutrophil in the second field is dysplastic, with hypogranular cytoplasm and abnormally clumped, irregularly segmented nuclear lobes. In the setting of cytopenias with 4% circulating blasts, the findings are consistent with myelodysplastic syndrome with excess blasts (former RAEB-1, 2–4% blood blasts), pending marrow evaluation.

ddx.vs: PMF also shows teardrop cells, nRBCs and occasional blasts, but typically with splenomegaly, JAK2/CALR/MPL mutation and marrow fibrosis rather than prominent neutrophil dysplasia.
Myelophthisis gives a leukoerythroblastic smear with teardrops but neutrophils are not dysplastic and tumor cells are found on marrow biopsy.
AML is diagnosed with ≥20% blasts in blood or marrow, whereas only rare blasts are present here.
Megaloblastic anemia shows macro-ovalocytes and hypersegmented neutrophils with normal granulation rather than hypogranular neutrophils and circulating blasts.
